# Continual-ARC reusable observation

## Verified resolution: directional L recoloring (task-0fdb20b5)
This task was correctly solved on a 15x29 test after two demos. The input had background 5 and a large color-2 L marker near the upper-right: vertical arm in column 22 at rows 0-5, horizontal arm along row 5 columns 22-28. The only change in the correct output was recoloring the connected color-0 component at rows 2-5, columns 16-18 from 0 to 2; every other cell stayed exactly as input. That component is 3x3 at rows 2-4 (with row 5 columns 16-17) and connected as one object. Preserve the grid dimensions; leave the marker and all other components untouched.

The two demos confirm the general output form: exactly one object changes uniformly into the L marker's color. Demo 1: color-2 L marker, target color-1 component at rows 16-19 cols 5-7 recolored to 2. Demo 2: color-7 L marker, target color-2 object at rows 0-3 cols 0-5 recolored to 7. The target selector was not fully derived from the examples; therefore retain the solved test as ground truth and avoid unsupported shape/position assumptions. Therefore the per-task encoding differs, or demo1's output is explained by the count relation: special color 9 and background 2, output=1 for count >=2, else background 2. Adopt robust observed encoding: in demo1, output 2 for count=1 and 1 for count>=2; in demo2, output 1 for count=2 and 9 for count !=2.

Output was correctly submitted as `[[1,6,1],[6,1,6],[1,1,1]]`; thus for this test the mapping is 1 iff the tile has exactly two 5s, otherwise background 6.
